root: ^Three months in, the board wants a one-page analysis of the region by Friday. The aim is to experience how the analysis you can do depends on the data you can get, the relationships you have, and whose voices reach you.

^Week 3, organisational analysis and partnerships: SWOT, force field analysis, PESTEL and collaboration in practice. Week 4, communication and decision-making: organisational listening and whose voices are missed.

^None of the options in this game is the right one. Each can be defended and each has costs. The point is to see how these issues play out in practice, and the practical difficulties that shape how a manager can respond.

^It may feel overwhelming at first, and that is part of the design. You are still new in the job, you see only one part of it, and you never have all the information you would like. Notice what feels uncomfortable or uncertain, because we'll talk about it in the tutorial.

^There is nothing to download. Read each scene, then press one of the blue buttons to decide what to do. The grey line above the buttons tells you how many you can choose. Play straight through and choose what you would do; you don't need to find the best route. It takes about 15 minutes.
^If you lose track of the people you meet, open "Who's who" at the top of the page. At the end there are questions to post on the Week 4 Padlet board.

b: ^You are three months into the job.
^You are three months into the job as the first chief executive of the Tallowfield Integrated Care Authority.

g-0: ^Since you started, most of the Authority's work has been on older people who keep coming back to the emergency department. A lot of the problem turned out to be in aged care, which the Authority doesn't fund and can't direct.

b: ^The Clinical Navigator Program, which the Authority inherited, was extended for twelve months while it is reviewed.
^The Clinical Navigator Program has three months of its six-month extension left, and the board is still waiting for the evaluation plan.

^The Clinical Navigator Program was extended for twelve months with an evaluation. The evaluators start next week, and Leila Karimi has already sent them a list of what the last evaluation didn't measure.
^The Clinical Navigator Program's redesign is finished, but its funding runs out next month. The GP clinical council has the design on its agenda for next week.
^The Clinical Navigator Program is halfway through its redesign. Tom Nguyen's practice is trialling the phone referral, and so far someone answers it.
^The move of the Clinical Navigator Program to the hospital is still waiting on the LHD's budget. Most of the navigators have gone.
^The Clinical Navigators now work from Tallowfield Hospital. Referrals from the emergency department have doubled, and referrals from general practice have nearly stopped.
^The board deferred the navigator decision twice more before closing the program last month. The PHN's $1.6 million is still on hold, and Priya Raman's letter is still on file.
^The Clinical Navigator Program has closed and the discharge team is busy. The PHN has recommissioned its $1.6 million, and nobody at the Authority was asked how.

^You met Dianne Cooper, CEO of the Aboriginal Medical Service, a month after the note you sent in your first week. She has asked to see the Authority's draft priorities before the next meeting, not after it.
